mutants.reason: With bit_cnt!=1 the stop-bit branch (bit_cnt==1) is never taken, so the receiver hangs at bit_cnt=1: no word is presented, no frame/overrun error pulses, and rx_busy stays high.

data_reg is 9 bits and bit_cnt starts at 9, so there are only 8 shifts at line 105. The bit shifted into data_reg[8] would reach txd only on a 9th shift, which never happens. The stop bit comes from line 109. The shifted-in bit never reaches txd or any other port.

Inverting bit_cnt>0 makes the receiver run the idle/start-detect branch while a frame is in progress and ignore bit_cnt>0 once it is idle. Data sampling, frame completion and rx_busy are therefore corrupted and frames are not received.

The top bit of data_reg (the constant 1 loaded here) is never shifted out. Only 8 shifts occur, which output data bits 0..7, and the stop bit is driven separately by txd_reg<=1. Changing this bit has no effect at any port.
With bit_cnt!=0 the idle branch (s_axis_tready=1, accept data) runs mid-frame and never when idle. The transmitter would not accept words when idle, and the frame shifting logic is not reached.

With || the pending word's m_axis_tvalid is cleared when tready is high without tvalid, or when tvalid is high without tready. A pending word is dropped while tready=0, so the stall and overrun-keep behaviour break.
Inverting bit_cnt>1 swaps the data-shift and stop-bit branches. The last bit uses the shift path and the stop bit is not emitted correctly, so the txd frame is corrupted and bit timing changes.

Inverting the handshake term clears m_axis_tvalid whenever there is no handshake and keeps it when there is. A pending word is dropped under backpressure, and a transferred word stays valid and is delivered again.
With bit_cnt!=1 the stop-bit branch never fires, since bit_cnt==1 fails the condition. txd is never driven back to 1 for the stop bit, and the transmitter stays busy at bit_cnt=1.
Same effect as M05: the idle/accept branch is taken when bit_cnt!=0 and skipped when idle. The transmitter never accepts a word from idle and the frame logic is corrupted.
Inverting prescale_reg>0 removes the bit-period wait. The receiver samples at the wrong times, the prescale baud timing breaks, and frames are mis-received or give frame errors.
With !tvalid the transmitter starts a frame when no data is valid and ignores a valid word. A word is not accepted on a tvalid&&tready handshake, and spurious frames are sent.
